challenges.name: typed-ui-state-quiz
challenges.title: Which states can the catalog be in?
challenges.description: Two pieces of evidence from the catalog page: the boolean state that shipped, and a compiler error after the switch to a discriminated union.

questions.explanation: False. Each field is typed on its own, and nothing in the type relates them: two booleans, a nullable string and an array allow every combination, including loading and failed at once, or failed with no message. The spread in the search handler shows exactly how that happens: it sets isLoading and keeps whatever isError and courses were before. Only a union whose members carry their own fields, such as { kind: "loading" } | { kind: "error"; message: string } | ..., lets the compiler reject those combinations. The misconception is that precise field types give a precise state; they constrain each value, not how the values fit together.

True. After the error branch returns, state is narrowed to loading, empty or success, and only success has courses. If the code compiled (for example with a cast), a loading state would pass undefined to CourseGrid and an empty search would show an empty grid instead of the empty-state message: the same class of bug as the original incident. The fix is to handle every kind, ideally with a switch that ends in assertNever, not to silence the error with `as` or an optional field. The misconception is that such errors are the type system being fussy; here the compiler is listing the screens the component forgot.

challenges.name: derive-catalog-ui-state
challenges.title: Derive the catalog's UI state
challenges.description: The CodeDev catalog page used three booleans and showed "No courses found" while it was still loading and a blank page when the API failed. Its query hook now gives a request snapshot { status: "pending" | "error" | "success", isFetching, query, data?, error? } (error = { status, message }, status 0 for a network error or timeout). Write deriveUiState(snapshot), which returns exactly one of { kind: "loading" } | { kind: "error", message, canRetry } | { kind: "empty", query } | { kind: "success", courses, refreshing }. Rules, in order: status "pending" is loading. Status "error": a 401 gives the message "Your session has expired. Sign in again." and canRetry false; status 0, 408, 429 or 500-599, or no error object at all, gives "Could not load courses. Try again." and canRetry true; any other status gives the API's error.message and canRetry false. Status "success" with data missing or empty is empty, with the query trimmed; with courses it is success, with courses = data and refreshing = isFetching, so a background refetch keeps the list on screen. The test runner reads a list of snapshots as JSON and prints the UI state of each, with courses shown as their ids.
hints: Which field of the snapshot tells you whether there is a response at all, and should it be checked before or after you look at the number of courses?

Look at the three values of snapshot.status first (a switch on it narrows nicely), then, inside the error branch, at error.status, and remember that error can be missing. Inside the success branch, data can be missing too, and the query may contain spaces typed by the learner.

A similar mapping for a different screen, the leaderboard: { status: "pending" } -> { kind: "loading" }; { status: "success", isFetching: true, data: [3 rows] } -> { kind: "ranked", rows: those 3 rows, refreshing: true }; { status: "success", data: [] } -> { kind: "noScores" }; { status: "error", error: { status: 404 } } -> { kind: "error", message: the API's message, canRetry: false }. Note that "no rows" is decided only after the request has succeeded.
